preserved_windows_source_deltas.scope: Add only the Linux navigation-to-CASC edge to Cargo's flattened all-target graph; no registry identity or Windows target edge changes
Add only an explicit Linux shared-package dependency; Windows dependency and source pins retain their original scope

admission.single_codec: The producer and consumer use the same canonical V23 coverage and source-identity codec. The executable no longer owns a second implementation.
expected_facts: optional exact package context; required by the RustyCore consumer
checks: Linux rooted no-symlink files and shared package lock
complete canonical manifest, receipts, seals and artifact namespace
exact artifact lengths and SHA-256 values
build, locale, component, source, plan and producer context
canonical source identity and selected effective-parent closure
complete selected terrain-input eligibility recorded by the existing profile
exact global, written tile, declared empty tile and coverage inventory
MMap16 complete framing and canonical producer paths
not_proven: native Detour topology safety from framing or hashes alone

owned_read_batch.retained_tiles: Only explicitly requested tiles are retained. All package artifacts are still verified.
owned_read_batch.overrides: Caller limits may only reduce built-in ceilings. Retained allocation capacities and transient per-file reads are accounted separately from package metadata and from native allocations; these are logical limits, not RSS measurements.
owned_read_batch.availability: A recorded empty tile is distinct from a written tile. A coordinate outside the selected coverage is unavailable, never fabricated empty geometry.
owned_read_batch.publication: Owned bytes and validated metadata are returned only after the entire canonical verification operation succeeds.
owned_read_batch.later_loads: The RustyCore owner requires the initially admitted context and complete package summary/inventory on each later batch read. Native operations use owned checked bytes after the verification call returns.

native_ingress.format_gate: An explicit checked Detour7 ground-payload profile for the vendored 64-bit-reference ABI. It does not relabel v16 containers as legacy v15.
checks_before_native_allocation_or_tile_: exact little-endian header, positive bounded counts, checked section sizes and complete payload extent
ground polygon shape, referenced vertex and internal-neighbor indices
supported external-portal directions and representable portal arithmetic
detail mesh ranges and triangle indices
BV leaf indices, forward escape ranges and representable quantization
finite bounded numerical inputs and valid native tile coordinates
zero off-mesh payloads for this selected profile
global parameters, bounded native capacities and payload tile placement consistent with the admitted global container
native_ingress.limits: Caller-reduced resource policies reject before native entry; budgets are not silently increased to make an observed route complete.
native_ingress.query_budget_identity: An existing instance query retains its admitted node budget. A conflicting valid budget is an error; changing the budget requires explicit unload and reload.
native_ingress.legacy_behavior: The existing legacy format remains explicit. Admission of this profile does not transfer newer-build acceptance to legacy readers or older-build acceptance to build70450.

rustycore_owner.query_lifetime: Instance queries belong to their existing MMapData and are destroyed before its mesh. No second native mesh/query registry or Send/Sync relaxation is introduced.
rustycore_owner.execution: Construction, package reads, tile preparation and queries run on the existing dedicated native pathfinder owner thread, outside map/entity/session locks.
rustycore_owner.feature: Explicit opt-in library capability; no automatic server configuration or world-entry activation.
rustycore_owner.source_scope: Only the admitted selected map and its supplied coverage are queryable. Older terrain-library build gates and unrelated phase topology are not evidence for this profile.
rustycore_owner.format_paths: Original MMap16 global and underscore-separated tile names are consumed through the shared package API; no legacy filename fallback is attempted.
rustycore_owner.errors: Configured source, integrity, format, scope and native failures remain errors. They are not converted to a successful straight-line path or missing-data fallback.
rustycore_owner.status: Native query detail bits and partial outcomes remain visible. A successful native status alone is not a complete-route claim.
rustycore_owner.rollback: Failed preparation must not publish partial native ownership as a successfully prepared batch; unload/cleanup and repeated load behavior have explicit tests.

rustycore_publication.qualification_method: Retained unchanged-candidate workspace, hygiene, dependency and data-suite evidence plus pinned-reference database, SDK, world and consumer continuation; no single green general-final invocation.

required: shared-codec synthetic roundtrip and diagnostic regressions without removed registrations
public verifier and owned-batch positive and negative synthetic consumers
strict native ingress malformed-index, size, numeric, portal, detail and BV rejection cases before FFI
existing manager and actual library/worker consumer lifecycle, failure and repeated load tests
bounded private real package admission and manager/query evidence with guarded inputs
requalification of the changed shipped Linux source graph and reproducible package

executed.rust_acceptance_method: Retained full sweep plus corrected diagnostic test rerun and remaining-crate continuation; no single green workspace invocation claim.
executed.core_publication: draft PR 1454 published under the existing unchanged inherited-debt experimental exception; merge pending and general final rejection retained

distribution.frozen_status_prose: The archive retains earlier source-definition status and the draft SDK/consumer-limit wording. Later status prose and the corrected consumer limit are documentation-only; the qualified Rust product sources are unchanged.

non_claims: no full-world geometry or navigation acceptance
no new native Trinity parity claim
no server gameplay, creation or world-entry acceptance
no Windows delivery or release authorization
